ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Panama AML/CFT framework); Ley 41 de 2000 (Unidad de Analisis Financiero - UAF); Ley 70 de 2019 and Decreto Ejecutivo 79 de 12 de mayo de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales / Ultimate Beneficial Owner Register); Decreto Ejecutivo 201 de 2017 (PEP definition and enhanced due diligence rules); Resoluciones of the Comision Nacional contra el Blanqueo de Capitales (CNBC) prescribing CDD protocols; Law 32 of 1927 as amended (Sociedad Anonima corporate law).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport-issuing authority of the individual's country of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted to the Panamanian resident agent for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the foreign principal's jurisdiction of residence or incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, Incumbency, or Corporate Existence of any corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Ley 23 de 2015 and CNBC regulations; automatic pre-clearance screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and UBOs against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the EU consolidated asset-freeze list, and Panama domestic lists; mandatory Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification covering domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs using commercial databases and official gazettes; Enhanced Due Diligence and source-of-funds documentation required for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and cross-border wire-transfer rails (Swift_Wire, ACH_Direct); all screening evidence must be preserved in the resident agent's KYC file and be available to the UAF and CNBC upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panamá — Sistema de Registro en Línea (Panamá en Línea), official web portal: www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names must be expressed or transliterated in Latin script; Spanish or a foreign language is permitted, but a certified Spanish translation must accompany the statute when the registered name is not in Spanish; the name must not be identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to any existing registered name; the statutory corporate type must be indicated by an accepted suffix such as Sociedad Anonima, S.A., Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, Inc., or Limitada; the name must not violate public order, public morality, or the dignity of the State.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant or resident agent must file a written administrative appeal ('recurso de apelación') with the Registrador General of the Registro Público de Panamá within five (5) business days of formal notification, pursuant to Law 38 de 2000 (Régimen Administrativo); the appeal must annex comparative evidence of pre-existing registrations, trademark certificates, and any ministerial or regulatory authorization obtained for sensitive tokens, together with the applicable re-search fee; if the administrative appeal is denied, a further judicial remedy may be pursued before the Civil Circuit Court of the first judicial circuit; a fresh name reservation application with a modified or transliterated name may alternatively be filed through the online portal within the 30-day reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permissible for this license-exempt programmatic advertising platform; Law 32 de 1927, as amended by Ley 5 de 1988, requires only a Panamanian resident agent and a registered office maintained at the resident agent's address; no statutory requirement exists for physical premises, local staff, or equipment for a Sociedad Anonima engaged in non-regulated AdTech activities under Panama's territorial tax regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection below 10% for a low-risk standard-tier AdTech platform; inspection risk increases materially if the UAF or CNBC issues an AML risk flag, if the DGI conducts economic substance or UBO register audits, or if the registered address shows anomalies during registry or banking compliance reviews.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (General Corporation Law), Law 32 of 26 February 1927, as amended by Law 5 of 22 March 2023 and Law 52 of 2016; Book II, Title I (Articles 2-12: formation and capital; Articles 17-23: registered agent; Articles 30-42: directors) supplemented by Executive Decree 511 of 2015 for digital filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección Nacional de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Legal Entities Registration Directorate), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (notarial deed) or private-instrument equivalent under Law 5 of 2023, recorded as the Pacto Social y Estatutos in the Mercantile Section.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Sociedad Anónima; authorized capital is freely fixed by founders (standard default USD 10,000 in 100 ordinary shares). A 5% capital registration tax is levied on the subscribed capital (minimum USD 100; cap USD 5,000) payable at filing. No escrow or immediate disbursement requirement; shares may be subscribed without full payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], S.A. — WHEREAS the corporation has been validly constituted under Law 32 of 1927, the undersigned directors, constituting a quorum, hereby RESOLVE: FIRST: The subscription of all issued shares and the authorized capital structure stated in the Pacto Social are ratified. SECOND: The registered office is fixed at [Street Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and [Resident Agent Firm] is confirmed as Resident Agent. THIRD: [President Name] is appointed President, [Treasurer Name] Treasurer, and [Secretary Name] Secretary, each with full authority over banking, contracts, and tax filings. FOURTH: The officers are authorized to file the Aviso de Operación, obtain the RUC, and execute all ancillary regulatory filings. Approved unanimously this [Day] day of [Month], [Year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — online name availability portal (www.registropublico.gob.pa) or authorized Panamanian counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names in order of preference for similarity screening against the Folio Electrónico database. Upon clearance, obtain the formal name reservation certificate (Certificado de Búsqueda). Conduct the search by corporate counsel or licensed agent; results are valid for 30 days. A reserved name is locked for the applicant's exclusive use pending registration.
required_dossiers: Name search request form
Copy of promoter's passport or corporate ID
Power of attorney if promoter acts through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected for similarity, file an administrative reconsideration with the Registro Público or immediately substitute an alternate cleared name; no penalty attaches to refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Panamá for public-deed format, or licensed Panamanian attorney for the private electronic instrument under Law 5 of 2023.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles specifying corporate name, authorized capital, share classes, term (indefinite or fixed), initial directors, and registered agent clause. Execute the deed before a Panamanian notary or the private instrument in the presence of corporate counsel. Obtain the registered agent's signed Acceptance Letter. The document must be in Spanish; a certified English translation should be prepared for bank and counterparty use.
required_dossiers: Valid corporate name reservation certificate
Passport copies of all founders and initial directors
Resident agent acceptance letter
Statement of authorized capital and share subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For drafting or attestation defects, execute a notarial correction protocol (protocolo de corrección) before the same notary and re-instrument the affected clauses prior to registry filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Capital Registration Tax and Fiscal Stamp Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (treasury collection) or the Registro Público's integrated payment counter / Pagavía online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Calculate the 5% capital registration tax on the subscribed capital (e.g., USD 10,000 subscribed results in USD 500 tax; minimum USD 100, maximum USD 5,000). Issue the payment order, make payment, and obtain the official treasury receipt (recibo oficial). Acquire and affix the required fiscal stamps (timbre fiscal) to the executed deed where applicable.
required_dossiers: Executed notarial deed or private instrument
Capital subscription calculation sheet
Official tax payment receipt (recibo oficial de ingresos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If overpaid, submit a refund petition to the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) with the treasury receipt; underpayment is cured by paying the differential plus a nominal late surcharge before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Inscription at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección Nacional de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section), final folio opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the full notarial deed or Law 5/2023 private instrument together with proof of tax payment and the name certificate. Upon review, the Registry opens the corporate folio (inscripción) and issues the Certificado de Registro, which evidences legal personality. Standard processing is sequential; expedited (same-business-day) service may be requested at an additional fee.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed or digital private instrument
Name reservation certificate
Tax payment receipt
Resident agent acceptance letter
Simple copy of promoter identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query (razón de no inscripción), cure the formal defect via notarial correction within 10 business days; a denial may be appealed administratively within 5 days under the Registro Público's internal appeal procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting: Officer Appointment, Registered Office, and Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private corporate act of the Board of Directors; no public registry filing is required, but records must be maintained at the registered office and accessible to the Resident Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent adopting the First Board Resolution. Issue subscribed share certificates, open the statutory share ledger and minute book (registered in the Libro de Registro de Acciones), adopt the corporate seal, and confirm the registered office address with the Resident Agent. Officer appointments are effective upon adoption and are not publicly filed.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution / minutes
Share subscription list and share certificates
Corporate seal invoice and specimen
Registered office lease or agent confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting or consent is procedurally defective, the board may adopt a ratifying resolution confirming prior acts; all signed consents are filed in the corporate minute book to evidence quorum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Commercial Operating License (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas for RUC; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) and Alcaldía de Panamá for the Aviso de Operación.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with DGI to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and apply for digital services exporter status where applicable. Submit the Aviso de Operación application via MICI's electronic window or the Municipality of Panama, evidencing the company's commercial premises, local representation, and proof of municipal tax readiness. For a pure-play AdTech/SSP platform no sector-specific industry license is required, but the Aviso de Operación is mandatory to commence revenue-generating operations.
required_dossiers: Certified Certificado de Registro from the Public Registry
DGI RUC registration forms
Copy of lease contract and utility bill for the premises
Fire safety inspection certificate (Cuerpo de Bomberos)
Copy of directors' and officers' identification
Notarized power of attorney for the local representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects the Aviso de Operación, appeal to MICI's Ventanilla Única as the appellate authority; correct any documentary deficiencies (e.g., zoning certificate) and resubmit within 5 business days without loss of priority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección Nacional de Empresas, in coordination with the Alcaldía de Panamá (Municipality of Panama) for the Aviso de Operación; no industry-specific AdTech license is imposed by Panamanian law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Commercial Operating License / Business Permit) issued through MICI's electronic business registry and municipal collection window.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Reglamentación y Evaluación Ambiental (DIREA), applying the Sistema de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental under Law 41 of 1998 and Executive Decree 57 of 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Registro de Operación, low impact registration) — office-based administrative and digital platform activities with no industrial discharge; not subject to a full EIA Report (Category II/III exempt as to this business scope).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, stacking emissions, or VOC discharge generated by a programmatic advertisement SSP platform; domestic sewage routed to the municipal IDAAN sewer system per COPANIT standards; electronic waste (servers, monitors, UPS batteries) must be handled under MiAMBIENTE waste management protocols; any emergency diesel generator (if installed) must comply with air-quality limits of Executive Decree 5 of 2012 (settable maximum 90 mg/m³ particulate matter for diesel units).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Certificado de Seguridad contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá covering egress, extinguishers, and alarm systems; structural load inspection by the Municipality of Panama building code office; workplace operating clearance from MITRADEL under the Programa de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional, including the mandatory occupational health registration with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and first-aid readiness for the office workforce.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), República de Panamá; primary portal: SITIO — Sistema Integrado de Trámites en Línea (https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa); export customs interface: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) at https://www.ana.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama S.A. obtains its RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) as follows: (1) incorporate through a licensed registered agent, recording the sociedad anónima in the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) file the Aviso de Operación with DGI prior to commencing business; (3) submit notarized corporate charter, appointment of the resident agent and legal representative, the representative's digital certificate (firma electrónica/token), and the Panamanian registered office address via the SITIO portal to request the RUC; (4) complete ITBMS registration and elect the electronic invoicing modality. Non-resident persons without a local establishment obtain a non-resident RUC for withholding-reporting purposes only; no active-business registration is triggered solely by passive foreign ownership of shares.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No pass-through or check-the-box election exists under Panamanian domestic law; a Sociedad Anónima is irrevocably an entity-level taxpayer and is a per-se corporation for U.S. check-the-box classification purposes. Available statutory elections: (a) consolidated income-tax filing for affiliated Panamanian entities under Article 704 of the Código Fiscal with DGI pre-authorization; (b) small-taxpayer simplified ITBMS regime for annual gross revenue at or below B/.36,000; (c) special Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime for qualifying regional service-export income upon favorable resolution by the competent commission; (d) declarations and regime-alignment filings under Law 254 of 2021 for international tax transparency, which do not create elective entity classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, a value-added tax under Law 38 of 2000 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de-minimis threshold: any person habitually transferring movable goods or providing services in Panama must register for ITBMS. Optional small-taxpayer (pequeño contribuyente) simplified regime applies to annual gross revenue not exceeding B/.36,000 (Balboa, at parity with USD 36,000), substituting full ITBMS with a reduced flat-rate contribution.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under DGI Resolution No. 201-5874 of 2019: all active ITBMS taxpayers must issue invoices through DGI-authorized billing software integrated to SITIO via SOAP/REST APIs using a qualified digital certificate. The online modality requires real-time DGI fiscal clearance, with a validation response, authorization code, and fiscal QR (eCódigo/digital stamp) that must appear on every invoice before delivery to the client. Paper and fiscal-printer documents are no longer accepted for non-micro taxpayers; monthly electronic transmission of purchase and sales ledgers to DGI is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to: (a) exports of goods physically leaving Panama, evidenced by customs DUA exit; (b) exports of services, including digital and programmatic AdTech services, where the service is rendered to and the benefit is exclusively realized by a non-resident party outside Panama and the service is not exploited in Panama. The programmatic DSP/SSP platform qualifies for zero-rating on services provided to non-resident advertisers, agencies, or exchanges; services to Panamanian resident advertisers or campaigns targeting Panamanian consumers are taxable at 7% and cannot be zero-rated. The exporter may claim refund or credit of embedded ITBMS input tax (crédito fiscal) on costs attributable to the zero-rated exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Declaración Única de Aduanas) with ANA exit validation
Commercial invoice and, for service exports, signed contract (MSA/insertion order) with the non-resident counterparty
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for goods; for services, delivery report, service logs, and geo-targeting/usage evidence proving offshore benefit

Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 bank confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a Panamanian bank account (Panama has no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is documentary best practice for DGI/ANA audit review)
ITBMS export register and input-VAT (crédito fiscal) reconciliation for the relevant monthly period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit limitation period is generally 5 years from the statutory filing deadline, extendable to 6 years for omissions or errors. Zero-rating claims are scrutinized on residency, place-of-performance, and place-of-benefit; documentary deficiencies trigger retroactive assessment of ITBMS at 7%, monthly moratory interest at the statutory rate, and fines from 10% up to 100% of the omitted tax for grave infractions. Fraudulent zero-rating or refund claims constitute tax evasion under the Código Fiscal and Law 254 of 2021, exposing the company and its legal representative to criminal penalties including imprisonment up to 5 years, joint liability of the resident agent, and retrospective clawback of refunded ITBMS credits with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not maintain a central bank or a dedicated foreign-exchange administration. The competent banking and AML/CFT supervisory authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); fiscal agency for the Republic is exercised by Banco Nacional de Panamá. The US Dollar circulates as legal tender and the Panamanian Balboa exists solely as a unit of account pegged at par.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully dollarized jurisdiction with de jure and de facto full convertibility across both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no prior approval requirements, and no surrender or conversion obligations applicable to dividend remittances, management fees, royalties, or equity repatriation. Profit remittance is unrestricted and subject only to ordinary AML/KYC documentation and Panama's territorial tax reporting rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama's legal framework imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender requirement for export proceeds or any inbound foreign receipts. Revenues derived from programmatic advertising, SSP, and DSP services may be retained freely in US Dollars or any other convertible currency in Panamanian or offshore bank accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, restricted to secondary disbursement rails. Panama's removal from the FATF grey list in October 2023 materially improves acceptance, yet EU/UK/Asia-Pacific EMIs frequently apply enhanced due diligence to Panama-domiciled S.A. entities because of residual offshore-vehicular perception. Legal constraints include the absence of a Panamanian EMI passporting regime and the requirement that the primary treasury relationship remain with a licensed Panamanian bank. EMIs are acceptable for low-value publisher payouts and multi-currency float segregation but should not substitute for local commercial banking in capital escrow or major settlement flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one director or authorized signatory is generally required by SBP-regulated first-tier banks for the initial due-diligence interview. Remote opening remains feasible in several institutions on a discretionary basis through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney, local-counsel attestation, video identification, and enhanced documentary review, particularly for low-risk non-financial corporate clients. Beneficial owners must be disclosed to SBP standards regardless of onboarding modality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity inherent to the Panamanian S.A. structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: DGI final beneficial-owner registry filing receipt, Registro Público de Panamá legajo and corporate certificate, apostilled certificate of incumbency, certified copy of bylaws and share register, and an ownership chain chart identifying all natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legacy offshore center and tax-haven jurisdiction flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of substantive commercial operations: executed programmatic ad-exchange and SSP agreements, platform licensing and SaaS documentation, office lease agreements, payroll and employee records, DGI income-tax returns, and a certified Paz y Salvo tax-clearance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth verification for capital injections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IFRS audited or reviewed financial statements, six to twelve months of shareholder bank statements, documented board resolutions approving capital contributions, prior-year tax receipts, and notarized declarations of source of funds and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) classification or sanctions-list screening ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn PEP declarations from all natural-person beneficial owners, executed OFAC/EU/UN sanctions-screening consent forms, certified passport copies plus a second government-issued identification document, and, where warranted, a Panamanian counsel legal opinion clarifying PEP status or reputational exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification as a virtual-asset business or regulated money-service activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Narrative and technical documentation confirming zero crypto-asset exposure and no money-transmitter or value-storage activity, a platform AML/KYC policy covering counterparty due diligence, independent compliance or penetration-test reports, and contracts with institutional DSP/SSP clients evidencing the expected settlement profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital contributions are routed via SWIFT MT202 or MT103 wire transfers from the contributing entity through its US correspondent bank to the beneficiary Panamanian bank. Owing to full dollarization, no central-bank approval, exchange-control registration, or investment permit is required. The MT103 field 70 should state 'Capital Contribution / Equity Funding' and field 72 should reference the shareholder resolution; the receiving bank will independently request the corporate resolution, updated incumbency certificate, and source-of-funds evidence before clearing the credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: US-dollar settlements to publishers, SSP partners, measurement vendors, and operating counterparties are cleared through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for cross-border payees and through Fedwire/CHIPS for US-based receiving institutions. Domestic Panamanian payees are serviced through the Panamanian ACH and local check clearing operated under SBP oversight. Commercial letters of credit are not a standard clearing rail for AdTech service revenue; programmatic settlement is executed on an open-account basis using trackable MT103 messages with UETR, consolidated batch files via host-to-host channels, and ISO 20022-compliant payment instructions where the bank supports them.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards against USD for liquid currencies (EUR, GBP, CHF, MXN, BRL) executed through licensed Panamanian banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted Latin American and Asian currencies (e.g., ARS, CLP, COP, CNY) transacted through international banking desks
Cross-currency swaps for longer-tenor multi-currency balance-sheet exposure, predominantly EUR/USD and GBP/USD
FX options (calls and puts) for directional treasury hedges within the bank's internal market-risk policy
Plain FX spot conversions permitted freely without any central-bank authorization as a consequence of Panama's dollarized monetary regime

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate franchise tax (Tasa Única Anual / TUA – USD 300 flat fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) jointly with the Registro Público de Panamá; payment channeled through Banco Nacional de Panamá or DGI online payment system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 March for calendar-year entities, covering each open operative year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 15 March triggers an administrative penalty of USD 150 for each overdue year; non-payment for 3 consecutive years authorizes the Registro Público to administratively strike off the entity and proceed with dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the deadline is 31 March of the following calendar year. Applicable only when the S.A. derives Panamanian-source income or conducts a taxable activity in Panama; an inactive vehicle remains subject solely to the TUA filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment penalties progressively accrue, including statutory interest at 10% per annum (prorated monthly), fines up to 100% of the tax due, and administrative enforcement actions by DGI; persistent noncompliance may result in tax liens, asset freezes, and referral for strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified independent audit by a Panamanian licensed CPA firm is mandatory when the entity's annual gross revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 or when total assets exceed USD 1,000,000; further audits may be compelled by DGI where the taxpayer is classified as high-risk or the corporate books are used as basis for tax assessments.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted and issued by the IASB, applied through Panamanian GAAP; smaller entities may present financial statements under the simplified framework recognized by DGI and the Panamanian Institute of Certified Public Accountants (NICCPA standards).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public annual UBO filing is required for shareholding transfers under the S.A. statutory regime; however, the licensed registered agent must obtain and retain a written annual certification of beneficial ownership for each entity, and every share transfer must be recorded immediately in the statutory Register of Members with date, number of shares, transferor/transferee details, and supporting endorsement. Directors are civilly liable for incomplete registers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,500 per year for a licensed registered agent including physical registered office, TUA filing processing, and forwarding of official notices
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500–3,500 for a dormant entity; USD 3,500–10,000+ for an operating AdTech holding vehicle requiring full IFRS audit and consolidation-level validation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxable; foreign-source programmatic advertising revenue is generally outside the Panama tax base. Qualifying SEM (Multinational Headquarters) entities may benefit from a 5% effective rate on eligible intra-group services; Ciudad del Saber and free-zone regimes may yield 0% on specified licensed activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 130 (Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) / DGI electronic filing portal (e-Tax / Declaración de Impuestos por Internet)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (final return); estimated quarterly prepayment obligations apply for taxpayers above the annual threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return must be filed within 3 months after each fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, the deadline is 31 March. Quarterly estimated payments are due on the 15th day of the 3rd month after each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from Panama-source operations and commercial transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue from Panamanian sources; foreign DSP/SSP mediation fees booked abroad should be excluded unless sourced to Panama under the nexus rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income and exemptions (foreign-source revenue, treaty-exempt royalties, SEM-free income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a source analysis memo and supporting contracts to prove the ad-exchange activities are consummated outside Panama; keep server logs and commercial agreement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductible costs and expenses, adjusted for transfer pricing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure related-party charges to ultimate parent for ad-tech, data, and IP services comply with the Arm's Length Standard and are substantiated by invoices and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at the statutory rate of 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities, use the tax treaty rate if applicable; otherwise, verify Panama-source allocation before applying any rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credits, and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is available for Panamanian tax on foreign-source income; only Panamanian-source withholding credits or prepayments can be deducted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 10% of the tax due; a 10% monthly surcharge on outstanding tax accrues for non-payment. Failure to file may lead to DGI official assessment, fines up to USD 25,000, and cancellation of taxpayer registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends distributed from earnings that have borne 25% CIT; 10% when the distributing company's earnings were taxed at a reduced or exempt rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC / Constancia de Residencia Fiscal) from the DGI and deliver it to the Panamanian withholding agent. The withholding agent must file the reduced-rate relief application with DGI before distribution; no treaty relief may be claimed unless the recipient demonstrates beneficial ownership and economic substance in its residence country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory WHT on payments to non-residents for use of IP/software in Panama; interest: 6% statutory WHT on cross-border debt interest. Under Panama's limited DTA network, treaty rates may reduce royalties to 5%-10% and interest to 0%-5%; however, the US and most major ad-tech hubs have no comprehensive DTA with Panama, making the statutory rates the default.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 2,000,000 (annual gross related-party transactions) triggers the Local File and Master File documentation duty; Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue equal to or above USD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 70 of 2019 (Economic Substance Regulations, ESR) broadly applies to Panama-incorporated entities deriving 'relevant income' from services, financing, leasing, and holding activities. An AdTech SSP/DSP that book-keeps finance and central management in Panama must maintain physical premises, full-time employees, and substantive decision-making in the Republic; pure 'shell' holding of IP or ad contracts is treated as non-compliant and a red flag for DGI and AML authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to include Panama-source ad-exchange revenue in Form 130, fabrication of deductible expenses, or concealment of bank balances in Panamanian accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal Code Articles 711-712: fine of one to three times the evaded tax plus interest and surcharges; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years; seizure and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly civilly liable to the unpaid amount, with a discretionary 50% penalty; travel bans are common for outstanding fiscal debt exceeding USD 10,000, and a conviction triggers disqualification from serving as director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panama S.A. solely as a passive holder of foreign programmatic advertising contracts, with no staff, premises, expense evidence, or management in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR violations attract fines up to USD 1,000,000, suspension of the tax-resident certificate, and the Commercial Registry may strike the entity off without judicial process.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute false substance declarations may incur personal fines, be removed from the registry of suitable directors, and face civil claims from creditors if the veil is pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or deemed distributions (including excessive non-arm's-length management fees to a foreign holding entity) without applying the 5%/10% dividend WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The distributing company is jointly liable for the unwithheld tax, monthly surcharge of 10%, a 25% fixed fine, and interest; DGI may order encumbrances on bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who authorizes the transfer of funds without WHT becomes personally liable for the unpaid tax and can be placed on the DGI 'debtor watch list', triggering travel restrictions and personal enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an artificially low markup to the foreign ad exchange parent for brokerage services, or failing to prepare and file the required Local File by the deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income at 25%, plus a 3% monthly compounding penalty for late assessment, a documentation penalty of up to 1% of the cross-border transaction, and in fraud cases a 100% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Deliberately falsifying intercompany pricing or destroying transfer pricing records can result in personal criminal liability, disqualification before DGI, and confiscation of personal assets in the extent of the underpayment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing programmatic ad revenues through Panama-based bank/ACH rails without a complete KYC/AML file, knowingly accepting funds from ad-fraud networks, or failing to submit Suspicious Activity Reports under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML fines for legal entities range up to USD 1,000,000 per infraction for non-filing or inadequate systems; serious cases lead to forced liquidation and regulatory license withdrawal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be sentenced to up to 12 years for money laundering, receive individual fines up to USD 100,000, and be barred from acting as fiduciaries; the public registry can impose personal travel bans pending investigations.
